HSPM 401.description: Enrollment and topic to be approved in advance by advisor and instructor.
HSPM 401.subject: HSPM
HSPM 401.title: Independent Study

HSPM 412.description: Designed to serve as an introduction to economic principles and applications used in the health sector. The role economics plays in various aspects of health care, demand-side and supply-side factors and issues, how various health care systems are impacted.
HSPM 412.subject: HSPM
HSPM 412.title: Health Economics

HSPM 491.description: Emerging issues in Health Services Policy and Management. May be repeated for a total of 6 credit hours as content varies by title.
HSPM 491.subject: HSPM
HSPM 491.title: Special Topics in Health Services Policy and Management

HSPM 500.description: Provide students with overview of health services management, management techniques and the different roles and functions of the different health care services. Use of field trips and guest speakers from different health care providers.
HSPM 500.subject: HSPM
HSPM 500.title: Introduction to Health Care Management and Organization

HSPM 509.description: Overview of the delivery and financing of health care in the rural U.S., with emphasis on vulnerable rural populations and access to care.
HSPM 509.subject: HSPM
HSPM 509.title: Fundamentals of Rural Health

HSPM 510.description: Comparative health systems of the world including health system organization, management, financing, resource use and health outcomes.
HSPM 510.subject: HSPM
HSPM 510.title: Comparative Health Systems and Health System Efficiency, Effectiveness, Sustainability and Equity

HSPM 513.description: An introduction to data management in healthcare institutions for undergraduate students and non-HSPM major graduate students. Topics include the nature of medical data, legal protections surrounding such information, and basis strategies for managing information technology resources.
HSPM 513.subject: HSPM
HSPM 513.title: Issues in Health Care Information Management

HSPM 514.description: Overview of health services delivery in the United States, including organization and financing of health care, health insurance practices, primary and long-term care among other topics.
HSPM 514.subject: HSPM
HSPM 514.title: Introduction to Health Services Delivery and Policy

HSPM 530.description: Introduction to health care finance. Course will teach reimbursement structures, regulatory mechanisms, cost control, and related factors unique to healthcare organizations.
HSPM 530.subject: HSPM
HSPM 530.title: Finance in Health Administration

HSPM 700.description: An interdisciplinary perspective on the field of health administration. Philosophy concepts, and skills of implementation, management, and evaluation are presented and discussed. Principles in the practice of health administration are applied to identified problems and situations.
HSPM 700.subject: HSPM
HSPM 700.title: Approaches and Concepts for Health Administration

HSPM 702.description: Introduction to historical and contemporary health care programs and policy initiatives in the public and/or private sectors that help improve equity in health and health care appropriate to women, childhood, and adolescence.
HSPM 702.subject: HSPM
HSPM 702.title: Maternal and Child Health Programs and Policies: Past, Present, and Future

HSPM 706.description: Linkages among economic development, poverty, inequality and health. Direct and indirect effects of health in economic development.
HSPM 706.subject: HSPM
HSPM 706.title: Health and Economic Development: Interrelationships among health, poverty and economic progress

HSPM 707.description: The ethical dimensions of decision-making in health care delivery, administration and epidemiologic research. Provides ethical foundations for discussion of topics in health-related research and practice.
HSPM 707.subject: HSPM
HSPM 707.title: Ethical Issues in Health Care and Research

HSPM 708.description: Concepts and principles of economic evaluation and applications of evaluation techniques (e.g., cost-effectiveness, cost-utility, cost-benefits, decision modeling) to the real-world issues and problems.
HSPM 708.subject: HSPM
HSPM 708.title: Methods of Economic Evaluation of Health Projects, Policies and Programs

HSPM 709.description: Analysis of issues and demographic, economic, and political forces affecting health care delivery systems in rural America. Examines structure of federal and state public health programs that impact rural health.
HSPM 709.subject: HSPM
HSPM 709.title: Perspectives in Rural Health

HSPM 710.description: Overview of the organization, financing, and delivery of health care services in the United States. Major topics covered include factors that have shaped the existing health care system, health care organizations and providers, public and private health insurance, access, cost, and quality of health care, health policy, and health reform efforts.
HSPM 710.subject: HSPM
HSPM 710.title: Introduction to the US Health Care System

HSPM 711.description: Introduction to the public policy process with an emphasis on policy formation, implementation, and impacts, as well as the role of various public and private stakeholders in the context of health care policies and programs at both the state and federal level; Overview of major models of policymaking; Examination of current health legislation.
HSPM 711.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in HSPM 710.
HSPM 711.subject: HSPM
HSPM 711.title: Health Policy

HSPM 712.description: Introduction to the application of tools from theoretical and empirical economics to issues related to health, health care, and health policy. Major topics covered include demand for health and health care, supply of health care services, health insurance, externalities, technological change in the health care sector, and health policy.
HSPM 712.subject: HSPM
HSPM 712.title: Health Economics

HSPM 713.description: Understanding and optimizing the use of health information systems and allied technologies including electronic medical records to improve healthcare organizations' performance in the areas of care delivery, operations management, quality, safety, and accessibility of healthcare services.
HSPM 713.subject: HSPM
HSPM 713.title: Information Systems in Health Administration

HSPM 715.description: Overview of health services research as a discipline with an emphasis on foundational work in the field, as well as contemporary issues in health policy and practice. Introduces students to conducting systematic literature reviews and using conceptual models to develop hypothesis-driven research questions designed to address a knowledge gap.
HSPM 715.subject: HSPM
HSPM 715.title: Introduction to Health Services Research

HSPM 716.description: An introduction to quantitative methods and analytical techniques with application to health administration. The course includes the use of models and simulation for decision making and control in health administration.
HSPM 716.subject: HSPM
HSPM 716.title: Quantitative Methods for Health Administration

HSPM 718.description: Strategy and tactics of state, regional, institutional health services planning. Special attention to the role of marketing.
HSPM 718.subject: HSPM
HSPM 718.title: Health Planning

HSPM 722.description: Sociological approaches to the study of health and the decision to seek health care.
HSPM 722.subject: HSPM
HSPM 722.title: Sociology of Health for Health Services Managers I

HSPM 723.description: Sociological approaches to the study of health care institutions.
HSPM 723.subject: HSPM
HSPM 723.title: Sociology of Health for Health Services Managers II

HSPM 724.description: Legal basis for health care activities; health care provider laws, regulations, antitrust and organizational governance.
HSPM 724.subject: HSPM
HSPM 724.title: Health Law

HSPM 725.description: A study of the current problems, theories, models, and strategics associated with managing human resources in the health care sector.
HSPM 725.subject: HSPM
HSPM 725.title: Human Resources Issues in Health Care Sector

HSPM 726.description: Course addresses the significant legal and ethical issues in Public Health practice; basis for Public Health actions, authorities and limitations; role of the three branches of government in Public Health protection.
HSPM 726.subject: HSPM
HSPM 726.title: Applied Public Health Law for Administrators

HSPM 727.description: Advancing public health policy through design and implementation of a policy change campaign.
HSPM 727.subject: HSPM
HSPM 727.title: Advancing Public Health Policy

HSPM 730.description: Application of the principles of financial management to the systems involved in the delivery of health care.
HSPM 730.subject: HSPM
HSPM 730.title: Financing of Health Care

HSPM 731.description: Provides working knowledge of financial management techniques for managers in the health care sector.
HSPM 731.subject: HSPM
HSPM 731.title: Health Care Finance I

HSPM 732.description: Provides knowledge base and decision-making tools for financial management in health care organizations using financial management tools and principles.
HSPM 732.subject: HSPM
HSPM 732.title: Health Care Finance II

HSPM 733.description: Financial accounting and internal accounting for management decision-making, including cost determination, cost control, performance evaluation and financial planning.
HSPM 733.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Undergraduate course in accounting or competency in accounting through personal study of an undergraduate accounting text.
HSPM 733.subject: HSPM
HSPM 733.title: Health Care Management Accounting

HSPM 764.description: An overview of management and policy concepts and issues pertaining to long-term care facilities and programs.
HSPM 764.subject: HSPM
HSPM 764.title: Long-Term Care Administration

HSPM 765.description: Seminar on theory of and practice of leadership as a manager in the health care industry.
HSPM 765.subject: HSPM
HSPM 765.title: Leadership in Health Care Organizations

HSPM 766.description: Human Resources Management in health care and allied topics.
HSPM 766.subject: HSPM
HSPM 766.title: Health Services Administration I

HSPM 768.description: Operations management in health care, supply chain management and logistics processes, health services process improvement.
HSPM 768.subject: HSPM
HSPM 768.title: Health Services Administration II

HSPM 769.description: To explore organizational behavior at the micro level (individuals, motivation, leadership, conflict management) and macro level (social systems, inter-organizational relationships, change and innovation, performance and strategy, organizational design), with particular focus on health care environments.
HSPM 769.subject: HSPM
HSPM 769.title: Organizational Behavior

HSPM 770.description: Case study format where students identify problems, evaluate alternatives and make decisions using health care leaders in the community to prepare cases. Integration of principles learned in other health care theory and management courses.
HSPM 770.subject: HSPM
HSPM 770.title: Decision Making For Health Care Executives

HSPM 772.description: Overview of international health status, demographics; communicable/noncommunicable diseases; health care needs, financing, and infrastructure delivery; and maternal and child health, family planning, and public health programs.
HSPM 772.subject: HSPM
HSPM 772.title: International Health

HSPM 774.description: Systems approach to quality management focusing on Lean and other quality management methods that can be directly applied in a healthcare setting. Group projects in local acutecare settings allow students to practice quality management skills.
HSPM 774.subject: HSPM
HSPM 774.title: Quality Management in Healthcare

HSPM 775.description: Principles and tools of epidemiology applied to decision-making in a health care environment. Knowledge and skills useful to health services managers related to statistics, population health management and assessment of medical care processes/outcomes are taught.
HSPM 775.subject: HSPM
HSPM 775.title: Managerial Epidemiology and Statistics in Healthcare

HSPM 776.description: Builds on prior MHA coursework on health care management to focus on specific knowledge and skills applicable to the management of physician practices.
HSPM 776.subject: HSPM
HSPM 776.title: Physician Practice Management

HSPM 777.description: Demand, supply, employment-based coverage, government-sponsored programs and managed care.
HSPM 777.subject: HSPM
HSPM 777.title: Healthcare Policy and Principles of Health Insurance

HSPM 778.description: The principles of marketing applied to the health care setting.
HSPM 778.subject: HSPM
HSPM 778.title: Health Care Marketing

HSPM 788.description: Applied public health practice experience addressing management or policy need in public health setting.
HSPM 788.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in all of the following courses: PUBH 725, PUBH 726, PUBH 730, PUBH 735, and 6 additional hours HSPM courses.
HSPM 788.subject: HSPM
HSPM 788.title: Applied Practice Experience

HSPM 791.description: Content varies by title. Course my be repeated for a total of 6 credit hours.
HSPM 791.subject: HSPM
HSPM 791.title: Selected Topics

HSPM 796.description: Synthesis of foundational and HSPM MPH competencies in preparing a high quality grant proposal to address a public health problem.
HSPM 796.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in all of the following courses: PUBH 725, PUBH 726, PUBH 730, PUBH 735, HSPM 712, HSPM 730, and HSPM 768.
HSPM 796.subject: HSPM
HSPM 796.title: Integrative Learning Experience

HSPM 797.description: On-site management project in a health care setting.
HSPM 797.subject: HSPM
HSPM 797.title: Management Residency

HSPM 798.description: Practicum in approved public health, community health, or health care setting emphasizing evaluation and service delivery planning or a project such as resolution of a management problem or evaluation of a program component.
HSPM 798.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: EPID 700, BIOS 700 and three additional hours in the major.
HSPM 798.subject: HSPM
HSPM 798.title: Public Health Residency

HSPM 800.description: This course uses a mixture of didactic presentations and seminar-style discussions to expose doctoral students to contemporary research in the field of health services policy and management and introduce various topics related to professional development. For advanced doctoral students, presenting at least once in this course will count towards satisfaction of the teaching requirement and is strongly encouraged.
HSPM 800.subject: HSPM
HSPM 800.title: Doctoral Seminar

HSPM 805.description: Introduction to the research process and the fundamental research designs commonly used in health services research, including experimental, quasi-experimental, and non-experimental approaches. Other topics include ethical issues in conducting research, the historical development of human subject protections, and the Institutional Review Board.
HSPM 805.subject: HSPM
HSPM 805.title: Health Services Research Design

HSPM 810.description: This course prepares doctoral students for more advanced analytic methods courses by providing them with a foundation in statistical programming software and a variety of mathematical, statistical, and epidemiological concepts including matrix algebra, differential calculus, statistical inference, correlation, univariate and bivariate analysis, sensitivity, specificity, direct and indirect standardization, etc.
HSPM 810.subject: HSPM
HSPM 810.title: Fundamentals of Data Analysis

HSPM 811.description: Introduction to ordinary least squares regression and related concepts including endogeneity, multicollinearity, heteroskedasticity, autocorrelation, and hypothesis testing. Application of concepts using statistical programming software.
HSPM 811.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in HSPM 810.
HSPM 811.subject: HSPM
HSPM 811.title: Linear Regression Models

HSPM 812.description: Overview of econometric methods for analyzing panel data using quasi-experimental designs including difference-in-differences, event studies, regression discontinuity designs, interrupted time series, and two-stage least squares/instrumental variables. Other topics include complex survey design, approaches to missing data, factor analysis, and specification tests. Application of concepts using statistical programming software.
HSPM 812.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in HSPM 811.
HSPM 812.subject: HSPM
HSPM 812.title: Panel Data Analysis

HSPM 813.description: Overview of regression models using maximum likelihood estimation and other non-linear approaches to analyze non-continuous dependent variables. Topics include logit, probit, ordered and multinomial models, count models, censored data, two-part models, and specification tests. Application of concepts using statistical programming software.
HSPM 813.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in HSPM 812.
HSPM 813.subject: HSPM
HSPM 813.title: Categorical Data Analysis

HSPM 815.description: Overview of qualitative and mixed methods approaches to answering health services research questions. Topics include grounded theory, phenomenology, semi-structured interviews, focus groups, ethnography, observation, case studies, content analysis, transcription and coding. Strengths and weaknesses of different approaches are discussed.
HSPM 815.subject: HSPM
HSPM 815.title: Qualitative and Mixed Methods in Health Services Research

HSPM 818.description: The course foci is on theories and techniques used in conducting economic evaluations and policy analyses to ascertain the efficacy and effectiveness of public health and health care programs, services, and policies. Enrollment is restricted to DrPH or PhD students.
HSPM 818.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: HSPM 711, HSPM 712, HSPM 845 and HSPM 846.
HSPM 818.subject: HSPM
HSPM 818.title: Economic Evaluation and Policy Analysis of Health Services

HSPM 820.description: The course is designed to give students knowledge and skills necessary to demonstrate leadership in a variety of public health venues. Course content will focus specifically on theories, skills, styles, and techniques used in providing leadership to public health and healthcare programs, services, and policy development, and research. Enrollment Restrictions: Students must be accepted into a PhD, DrPH, or MPH program.
HSPM 820.subject: HSPM
HSPM 820.title: Public Health Leadership

HSPM 830.description: Overview of secondary data sources commonly applied in health services research, such as population and provider-based surveys, electronic health records, claims data, and administrative data sources. Application of data management concepts using statistical programming software.
HSPM 830.subject: HSPM
HSPM 830.title: Secondary Data Sources for Health Services Research

HSPM 845.description: Readings and discussion of topics relevant to research in health administration/health sciences.
HSPM 845.subject: HSPM
HSPM 845.title: Advanced Study in Health Policy Management I

HSPM 846.description: Readings and discussion of’ major topics, including institutionally based issues, in research in health administration/health sciences.
HSPM 846.subject: HSPM
HSPM 846.title: Advanced Topics in Health Policy and Management II

HSPM 890.description: Directed research on a topic to be developed by doctoral student and instructor. May be repeated for credit.
HSPM 890.subject: HSPM
HSPM 890.title: Independent Study

HSPM 898.description: Students are required to conduct applied public health methods and strategies as a part of their practicum experience. Examples of practicum include, but not limited to development, implementation, and evaluation of public health or healthcare services, policies, organizational development, and regulatory activities.
HSPM 898.subject: HSPM
HSPM 898.title: Doctor of Public Health Practicum

HSPM 899.description: One full year ,18 hrs, of graduate study beyond the master’s level.
HSPM 899.subject: HSPM
HSPM 899.title: Dissertation Preparation
